questions_and_answers.question_text: What does guǎn A jiào B mean?
What are the three levels of commune organization?
At which level are planning and payment handled?
What does -zhe describe when used with a verb?
Write the Chinese for "The door is open."
What does the name Sìjìqīng mean literally?
When were the people's communes formed, and from what?

answers.answer_text: In 1958, by merging several advanced agricultural cooperatives.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "It isn't written on the list."

articles.text:
1. A: Tāmen guǎn zhèige gōngshè      What do they call this commune? Is it
      jiào shénme? Dānzishang yǒu    written on the list?
      méiyou xiězhe?
   B: Xiězhe ne, jiào "Sìjìqīng."   Yes, it's called Sìjìqīng.

Notes on No. 1

guǎn...jiào...: GUǍN A JIÀO B means "to call A B."

Guǎngdōng rén guǎn qípáo jiào    Cantonese call qípáos (a kind of dress)
chángshān.                       "chángshān."

gōngshè: "commune." This is short for RÉNMÍN GŌNGSHÈ, "people's commune." Gōng means "public," and shè is an "organized body."

People's communes, of which there are now over 52,000 in China, are the ADMINISTRATIVE UNITS of the countryside. There are THREE LEVELS of commune organization:
  — the PRODUCTION TEAM, with from eleven to over one hundred households;
  — the PRODUCTION BRIGADE, with from twenty to over one thousand households; and
  — the COMMUNE itself, with from six to seventeen brigades.

A typical commune might have 22,500 people, broken into fifteen production brigades of three hundred families each, each brigade composed of ten production teams of thirty families.

The people's communes were formed after a long series of changes beginning with the LAND REFORM MOVEMENT of 1950, which distributed the land to the peasants. In 1951, MUTUAL AID TEAMS were formed — peasants still owned their own land but pooled manpower and tools. In 1953, ELEMENTARY AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES were organized; the land became property of the cooperative but profits were distributed. In 1956, ADVANCED AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES were established and profit distribution was abolished. In 1958, the PEOPLE'S COMMUNES were formed by merging several advanced cooperatives; what was formerly an advanced cooperative became a PRODUCTION BRIGADE. The original plan had called for completion in 1967; it was completed NINE YEARS AHEAD OF TIME.

Today, commune members still live in individual houses. All the land, buildings, shops, clinics, large machinery and factories belong to the commune. However, the PLANNING of production and the PAYMENT of members is done at the PRODUCTION TEAM level. Production teams often specialize in one type of activity. Production brigades handle tasks beyond a team's capacity, such as irrigation or purchasing a tractor. Truly large projects — road construction, a large hospital — must be taken on by the commune.

yǒu méiyou xiězhe: -ZHE is the marker of DURATION. Together with a verb it describes a STATE:

Mén kāizhe.                      "The door is open." (in the state of
                                 having been opened)
Mén guānzhe.                     "The door is closed."

Thus XIĚZHE means literally "in the state of having been written."

To make a verb plus -zhe NEGATIVE, use MÉI(YOU) — NOT bù:

Mén méi kāizhe.                  The door is not open.
Dānzishang méi xiězhe.           It isn't written on the list.

To make a QUESTION, use one of:
Mén kāizhe ma? / Mén yǒu méiyou kāizhe? / Mén kāizhe meiyou?

NE is often added to the end of a sentence with -zhe:
Mén kāizhe ne ma?                Is the door open?
Kāizhe ne.                       Yes, it's open.

Many speakers of Standard Chinese DO NOT USE this -zhe; they would say Mén kāile and Dānzishang yǒu méiyou xiě. These are also perfectly good Chinese.

Sìjìqīng: A commune in rural Běijīng. Literally the name means "four-seasons-green," in other words, "GREEN ALL YEAR ROUND."
